sections.overview: This marine elapid occurs in the Indo-West Pacific. Older literature also uses names such as Thalassophis viperina and Praescutata viperina.
sections.identification: SeaLifeBase records a maximum total length of 78 cm for males or specimens of unspecified sex.
sections.habitat: It is reported from coastal, reef-associated tropical waters, with records from 15–40 m depth.
sections.diet: The species is reported to feed on fish.
sections.behavior: Along the Indian coast, published records remain sparse and include strandings and fishing bycatch.
sections.reproduction: The Reptile Database describes it as ovoviviparous.
sections.ecology: Its ecology is poorly documented; a recent review specifically identifies major gaps in knowledge along India’s coast.
sections.conservation: SeaLifeBase reports a global Least Concern assessment dated 15 February 2009.

sources.title: Insights into the rare Viperine sea snake — Indian Journal of Geo-Marine Sciences
